newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts hold with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts hold with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures ended mixed Friday in a lackluster session, with front months clinging to modest gains amid reports of relatively firm bidweek cash prices, industry sources said.
June edged up 0.4 cent to close at $2.126 per million British thermal units. July settled 1.8 cents higher at $2.155. Others ended narrowly mixed, with 1999s lower.

"Cash was very strong (early), came off, then bounced back a bit. Futures (June) are trading between $2.10 and $2.20, and based on cash, anything below $2.10 is a buy and above $2.20 a sale," said one East Coast trader.
While some expected milder U.S. weather next week to pressure physical and paper prices into early May, few thought the market would collapse, with summer cooling loads just around the corner.
Technical traders still pegged support in June at $2.03 and then along the short-term up trendline in the $2.00 area. Resistance was seen at $2.24 and then in the $2.33 area.

In the cash, Henry Hub weekend prices firmed more than five cents Friday to the $2.15-20 level. May gas at the Gulf was up almost a nickel to the $2.10-15 area. April Midcon held relatively steady in the mid-$1.90s, with May on the same pipes up slightly to the mid-to-high $1.90s. April gas in New York gained more than five cents to the mid-$2.40s, while May city gate was up a couple of cents to the mid-$2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip rose 0.3 cent to $2.214. NYMEX said 30,944 Hub contracts traded, down sharply from Thursday's revised tally of 86,855.

On the KCBT, May expired 6.5 cents higher at $2.02, while deferreds ended up by one-half to two cents. The June East/West spread narrowed by 1.6 cents to 13.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 1,012 lots changed hands, up from Thursday's total of 661.
